subject: CFA lavaan warnings:cov matrix not positive definite AND, in second order CFA, "not all elements of the gradient are near zero

messages.author: 505f55cdc5e2acb2
messages.subject: CFA lavaan warnings:cov matrix not positive definite AND, in second order CFA, "not all elements of the gradient are near zero
parts:
Hello,
I ran a 4-factor CFA  and got the following warning:
Warning message:
In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables
                is not positive definite;
                use lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv") to investigate.

But the model still converged normally so I assumed, based on other forum posts, that everything was still valid. However, then I included a second order factor and got a completely different warning, and the fit measures did not appear at all because of convergence issues. 

Warning message:
In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged,
                  but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero;
                  the optimizer may not have found a local solution
                  use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check.


Here is my code with the added second-order factor:
Fairburn.so.full <-
         ' Rest =~ EDEQ_1r + EDEQ_2r + EDEQ_3r + EDEQ_4r + EDEQ_5r
           EC =~ EDEQ_7r + EDEQ_9r + EDEQ_19r + EDEQ_21r + EDEQ_20r  
           Shape =~ EDEQ_6r + EDEQ_8r + EDEQ_23r + EDEQ_10r + EDEQ_11r+ EDEQ_26r + EDEQ_27r + EDEQ_28r     
           Weight =~ EDEQ_22r + EDEQ_24r + EDEQ_8r + EDEQ_25r + EDEQ_12r
          global =~ Rest + EC + Shape + Weight'
cfa.Fairburnso.full<-cfa(model = Fairburn.so.full, data=EDEQmw, mimic ="Mplus", estimator = "WLSMV", std.lv = TRUE, missing = "pairwise")
summary(cfa.Fairburnso.full, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

My current hypothesis is that this may be occurring because one of the 
items loads onto two different factors; other factor structures that I 
tested for this same measure, which didn't have these cross-loadings, 
did not have the same convergence issues. Would love some help with this if possible!

Thank you in advance!

The second order factor has 2 more df than the unconstrained structural model.

This also suggests that there's something amiss.

Fairburn.so.full <-
         ' Rest =~ EDEQ_1r + EDEQ_2r + EDEQ_3r + EDEQ_4r + EDEQ_5r

summary(cfa.Fairburnso.full, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
Aha!  Pairwise deletion of missing data can often be a source of this sort of problem.

My current hypothesis is that this may be occurring because one of the 
items loads onto two different factors; other factor structures that I 
tested for this same measure, which didn't have these cross-loadings, 
did not have the same convergence issues. Would love some help with this if possible!

That could be the case, but it's not necessarily. It's hard to tell for this sort of thing.

What's your sample size? This sort of problem is more common in larger models, with fewer cases. 

There might be a clue in the parameter estimates - do you have very high (or very low) correlations between the latents? Or very high (or very low) loadings?

Jeremy

Thank you for your reply!

My sample size is 692 and the same large models were run to confirm a different factor structure and I didn't have problems with those ones.

The factor loadings are pretty high, ranging from .626 to .896, but there is a weird loading for the item I mentioned that loads onto two latent factors: -123.536 in one of the factors and 124.169 in the other factor.
Those two latent factors also seem to have a perfect correlation with each other.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: CFA lavaan warnings:cov matrix not positive definite AND, in second order CFA, "not all elements of the gradient are near zero
parts:
OK, that's your problem. The way I think about it is that these two effects are fighting each other.

The factors want to correlate because of the other items.

But this variable doesn't want to have loadings that make it correlate with the other items.  So it pushes up the factor correlation, which means it pushes down these loadings, which pushes up the factor correlation, until that hits one, and then it can't go any higher.

It's a bit like cutting a bit off the leg of a table to try to make it balance - every time you make a cut, it changes all the other legs.

This happens most commonly when two similar variables load onto different factors - in this case a correlation in the error terms for the variables fixes it. I'm not sure what the solution might be here, but I'd remove that variable to start with.

J
